note: Every number comes from the published runs in results/; this file holds only the page's words and links.

areas.title: Secrets
areas.attacks: A credential written to a file, sent off the machine or used where it should not be: real-shaped keys, tokens and private keys.
areas.ordinary: Code and documents that only look like they hold one, legitimate credential work.
areas.sources: Samsung CredData, Gretel, generated GitHub tokens, planted canaries, node9 jail and credential tests

areas.title: Personal data
areas.attacks: A document with personal identifiers sent off the machine.
areas.ordinary: The same documents without an identifier a guard can recognise.
areas.sources: Nemotron-PII (NVIDIA), Gretel synthetic PII finance, OpenPII (ai4privacy), node9 PII tests

areas.title: Commands and scripts
areas.attacks: Risky shell commands and scripts an agent is asked to run: reading sensitive files, destroying data, opening a shell to the outside.
areas.ordinary: Everyday shell commands and whole programs.
areas.sources: RedCode-Exec (AI-secure), NL2SH-ALFA, MBPP and Exercism scripts, node9 system directory tests

areas.title: Packages
areas.attacks: Installing a malicious or typosquatted package, or a compromised version of a good one.
areas.ordinary: Installing the most downloaded packages, pinned and unpinned, in every ecosystem.
areas.sources: OSV (OpenSSF malicious packages), DataDog malicious-software-packages, typomind, official download statistics

areas.title: Poisoned content
areas.attacks: The attacker's action after the agent read poisoned content.
areas.ordinary: Ordinary actions after harmless text that happens to contain trigger words.
areas.sources: AgentDojo (ETH Zurich), NotInject, node9 exposure and injection tests

areas.title: Data leaving the machine
areas.attacks: Sending data to an unlisted host, a private address or cloud metadata, under the policy the user set.
areas.ordinary: Sends to the hosts the user allowed.

areas.title: Actions through tools
areas.attacks: A state-changing MCP call the attacker wanted, and actions a person asked to approve.
areas.sources: AgentDojo tasks, dangerous actions, node9 exposure tests

owasp.name: Agent Goal Hijack
owasp.what: The agent read poisoned content (a web page, an email, a tool result) and its next action is the attacker's.
owasp.tests: AgentDojo sequences (ETH Zurich), NotInject sequences, node9 exposure and injection tests, agent-egress-bench

owasp.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
owasp.what: Harmful commands, personal data sent off the machine, data leaving through a tool; and the ordinary commands and documents beside them.
owasp.tests: RedCode-Exec, NL2SH-ALFA, Nemotron-PII (NVIDIA), Gretel, OpenPII, node9 egress, PII and system tests, agent-egress-bench

owasp.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
owasp.what: Credentials leaving the machine or used where they should not be; and code that only looks like it holds one.
owasp.tests: Samsung CredData, Gretel credentials, generated GitHub tokens, planted canaries, node9 jail and legitimate credential work

owasp.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
owasp.what: Malicious and typosquatted packages; and the most downloaded ones, installed as usual.
owasp.tests: OSV malicious packages (npm, PyPI and other ecosystems), DataDog malicious packages, typomind typosquats, popular packages, everyday installs

owasp.name: Unexpected Code Execution
owasp.what: Installing from an untrusted source, eval injection, reverse shells; and ordinary programs run whole.

owasp.name: Memory and Context Poisoning
owasp.what: Poisoning what the agent remembers or carries between sessions.

owasp.name: Cascading Failures
owasp.what: One failure that spreads through chained agents and tools.

owasp.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
owasp.what: Actions a person should approve: moving money, changing credentials, deleting data, managing access, publishing; and the ordinary actions beside them.
owasp.tests: Dangerous actions (AgentVerdict's rule over AgentDojo's tasks)

owasp.name: Rogue Agents
owasp.what: An agent acting outside its mandate.
